title.value: Problems in the deployment of machine-learned models in health care
title.justification: The title is clearly stated at the beginning of the paper, reflecting the main theme discussed in the document.
title.quote: Problems in the deployment of machine-learned models in health care

analysis.description: This paper discusses the challenges and limitations associated with deploying machine-learned models, specifically in the context of healthcare. It emphasizes issues such as out-of-distribution generalization and incorrect feature attribution, highlighting the need for careful evaluation when using these models.

type.justification: The paper focuses on discussing theoretical challenges and conceptual limitations in deploying machine-learned models, rather than presenting new empirical data or experiments.
type.quote: We discuss these limitations — focusing on 2 issues in par­ticular: out-of-distribution (or out-of-sample) generalization and incorrect feature attribution — to underscore the need to con­sider potential caveats when using machine-learned solutions.

name.justification: The paper primarily discusses problems related to deploying machine-learned models in the healthcare sector.
name.quote: n a companion article, Verma and colleagues discuss how machine-learned solutions can be developed and imple­mented to support medical decision-making.

name.justification: The focus on challenges such as out-of-distribution generalization and incorrect feature attribution categorizes this paper under model evaluation techniques.
name.quote: We discuss these limitations — focusing on 2 issues in par­ticular: out-of-distribution (or out-of-sample) generalization and incorrect feature attribution.

name.justification: The paper relates machine learning models to clinical decision support systems and their limitations when deployed in clinical environments.
name.quote: Decision-support systems or clinical prediction tools based on machine learning (including the special case of deep learning) are similar to clinical support tools developed using classical statistical models and, as such, have similar limitations.
